statusText: Mapped policy state: WATCH. Verified premarket reporting showed Nasdaq-100 futures about 1% higher after the Fed hike, but direct live NQ retracement quality remains unverified ahead of the 12:30 UTC data cluster.
recommendation: Mapped policy state: WATCH; the 12:30 UTC releases and subsequent cash-open sequence remain the main conditional danger window, with any escalation dependent on observed persistent directional extension.
headline: Nasdaq-100 remains in WATCH as the 12:30 UTC U.S. data cluster approaches
body: Verified premarket reporting showed Nasdaq-100 e-minis about 1% higher, with a softer 10-year Treasury yield and lower oil supporting equities. Event and geopolitical stress are extreme, while the absence of sufficiently current direct NQ retracement evidence keeps Tail below a blocking threshold.

lookbackSummary: Across the prior 24 UTC clock-hours, Tail peaked at 25% during the September 16 FOMC sequence, fell to 18-19% overnight, and then rose to 22% by 11:00 UTC as premarket strength increased.
outlookSummary: Current Tail is WATCH rather than blocked. Conditional Tail reaches upper WATCH through the 12:30 UTC data and cash-open sequence, then falls if meaningful retracements and two-way trade develop.

forecast.analysis: After the 12:30 UTC releases, upper WATCH is conditional on whether the initial move extends persistently; an orderly retracement would argue against a Tail escalation.
drivers: 12:30 UTC claims, housing and Philadelphia Fed releases

forecast.analysis: The cash-open hour keeps upper WATCH conditional on opening-auction continuation, shallow pullbacks or repeated failed retracements rather than on the data surprise alone.
Tail can ease from upper WATCH if the opening impulse becomes two-way after the 14:00 UTC Pending Home Sales checkpoint; renewed persistent extension would invalidate that decay.
A lower WATCH baseline applies if the early U.S. session develops meaningful two-way trade; session-extreme holding without retracement would keep risk above this path.
Tail falls below WATCH if pullbacks continue to interrupt directional runs; repeated extension after failed pullbacks would be the main contrary signal.
Low Tail is consistent with two-way afternoon discovery, while sustained directional efficiency without material retracement would challenge the baseline.
drivers: Retracement depth through the U.S. afternoon

forecast.analysis: Late-afternoon Tail remains low if price rotates away from extremes; persistent extreme-holding would keep a higher conditional path relevant.
The power-hour baseline stays low Tail if closing flows remain two-way; a renewed one-way drive would be the escalation condition.
After the U.S. cash close, Tail is low absent a new catalyst or a persistent post-close extension that carries the earlier directional move forward.
drivers: Persistence of the U.S. session move

forecast.analysis: Early post-close trade has a normal low-Tail baseline; geopolitical or rates headlines could reintroduce stress without automatically implying mean-reversion failure.
The evening baseline remains low Tail if no fresh directional catalyst emerges and cross-asset conditions avoid renewed alignment.
Early Asian-hours Tail remains low under a quiet handoff; a gap-like futures move with shallow retracements would be the main conditional escalation route.
A normal overnight baseline applies if futures remain rotational; persistent extension after failed pullbacks would move risk above this path.
Low Tail persists conditionally through the quieter overnight window, with stress still sensitive to rates and Middle East headlines.
drivers: Rates and Middle East headline sensitivity

forecast.analysis: The late-Asian baseline remains low Tail if price discovery is two-way and no cross-asset shock creates a fresh directional stack.
As Europe approaches, Tail edges higher only conditionally; a directional handoff with limited retracement would matter more than headline volatility by itself.
Early European trade keeps a modest Tail premium if index futures and rates begin to align directionally; mixed signals would support the lower path.
Tail remains low-to-moderate if European price action rotates; repeated extension with semiconductor and megacap alignment would challenge the baseline.
The European morning carries slightly higher conditional Tail as U.S. participation approaches, but persistent one-way structure would still need to be observed.
drivers: Observed one-way structure remains the escalation test

forecast.analysis: Tail stays below WATCH if the transatlantic handoff remains two-way; abnormal premarket gaps or failed retracements would raise the conditional path.
drivers: Abnormal premarket gap or failed-retracement checkpoint

forecast.analysis: U.S. premarket stress can rise ahead of Friday's data while Tail remains low unless directional efficiency and cross-asset alignment are actually observed.
drivers: Directional efficiency must be observed before Tail escalation

forecast.analysis: The premarket baseline keeps Tail low despite rising event stress; persistent extension or session-extreme holding would be required for a higher path.
drivers: Event stress ahead of Industrial Production

forecast.analysis: With Industrial Production and a Fed speech approaching later in the U.S. morning, Stress rises while Tail remains low absent observed mean-reversion failure.
drivers: 13:30 UTC Fed Vice Chair Bowman speech approaches

forecastDetail.comment: Premarket strength supports WATCH, but unverified live retracement quality keeps Tail below a blocking threshold.
The 12:30 UTC release cluster is a repricing checkpoint; upper WATCH depends on persistent post-release extension.
Cash-open continuation and failed opening pullbacks are the key conditional Tail tests.
Tail eases if the opening impulse becomes two-way after the 14:00 UTC housing checkpoint.
Lower WATCH assumes meaningful two-way trade and no sustained session-extreme holding.
Tail drops below WATCH if directional runs are interrupted by meaningful pullbacks.
